The readers

Two children read. Grade 3, English; grade 4, Urdu. 2026.

How we measure

Every term, our children and children in nearby schools sit the same test.

Reading

Low-fee schools, grades 1 to 3, 2023: 64% of our children read at grade level, 41% in the school next door. 50% more children reading at grade level.

Maths

When maths fell behind the schools next door, we sent the quiz home to parents on WhatsApp.

Islamabad

Public school classes, before and after one year with us: a gain of 0.28 standard deviations. Our own measurement, before and after; no outside study yet.

What a full trial would add

A comparison group chosen by lot, independent assessors, and the plan written before the results.

Working with the government

We learned who was in the government, and gave it the credit.

The people

Hundreds of officials mapped, by province; won over one at a time.

The brand

In Islamabad the programme carries the government’s name. The credit is theirs.

The data

Every officer sees which schools need help, and where it is working.

Appraisal

In Islamabad, our data now feeds teachers’ appraisals.

Today

Islamabad, paid since December 2023: 422 schools. Rawalpindi: 261 schools, $3 a child. Balochistan: winter schools. Sindh: a pilot.

Learning per dollar: the method

The measure

How much more a child learns, for every $100, in years of learning.

The table

86 programmes with a causal study behind them, ranked. Oxford, 2023.

The top

The first five rows train no teachers. Of the 12 that train teachers, Argentina is first at 15.4.

Our own figure

4.3 per $100 (4.25 before rounding): Islamabad, our own measurement, before and after, at $8.24 a child. No outside study yet; studies are planned for 2027.

Where we sit

Eight of the twelve programmes that train teachers score higher: ninth of thirteen.

The target

20 by the end of 2028: first among programmes that train teachers.

github.com/Orenda-Project/rumi-platform

Why the problem exists

Every child is born with the same potential. Three layers around them decide what happens to it.

The home

Parents who could not go to school themselves, working long hours, often speaking a different language from the one the school teaches in.

The teacher

Trained once in fifteen to twenty years. Fifty children in the room. No structured materials for teaching reading.

The government

Policy that changes with every government, and no data on which children are learning and which are not.

Taleemabad gives each one what it needs:
digital learning content in Urdu at home; lesson plans and coaching for the teacher;
data and policymaking support for the government.
